title: The Gospel of John
lead: The fourth Gospel, which tells the story of Jesus from "In the beginning was the Word" (John 1:1) to the risen Lord by the lake. This page is about the book: its authorship, date, stages of writing, purpose and relation to Matthew, Mark and Luke. For the people (John son of Zebedee, John the Elder, the Beloved Disciple), see the person page.

sections.b: About nine tenths of John has no parallel in the other three Gospels. Jesus has no parables of the kingdom and casts out no demons; instead he does seven "signs" and speaks in long conversations and speeches about himself, the Father and eternal life. He goes up to Jerusalem for several festivals, so the ministry spans about three Passovers (John 2:13; 6:4; 11:55), and he clears the Temple at the start (John 2:13–22), not in the last week (Mark 11:15–19).

The Gospel names no author but rests its story on the witness of the disciple Jesus loved (John 21:20–24). Irenaeus, about AD 180, says that John, the Lord's disciple who leaned on his chest, published the Gospel at Ephesus. Papias, earlier, names both the apostle John and a "John the Elder", and some scholars (Martin Hengel, Richard Bauckham) think the Elder is the Beloved Disciple. Many critical scholars think a circle of the disciple's followers finished the book in stages, adding chapter 21 at the end.
